review_scope: static: retail instructions and emitted candidate listing

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: 229 bytes, 80 instructions, entry 0x004B1420 through the single ret at 0x004B1504; the emitted candidate is 14 blocks / 21 edges, exactly retail's count.

checks.name: cfg_match
checks.rationale: Both decoders report 14/21 against retail's 14/21, score 1.000. The flow analysis had predicted 16/23 from a standalone -O3 compile of its draft; the project's actual flags emit 14/21, so its caveat does not apply to the landed build.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Three cdecl arguments (path, callback, context); the call site 0x00485150 pushes arg3 then 0x00484E60 then "LOCAL:missions" and cleans 0xC. The two saved-register reads at 0x004B144E/0x004B1455 are arg3/arg2, read once outside the loop.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: 0x004B1020 alias resolve twice, 0x004B11A0 index twice, one indirect call through record+0x00 with four dwords, two Debug_Error terminals that spin, and the return of the handler's EAX.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: Record stride derived exactly as retail: (index*8 - index)*5*4 = index*0x8C; present word at record+0x1C (0x00943708 with the scale applied); handler at record+0x00 (0x009436EC); five-record bound at 0x004B145F; both error strings byte-identical.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: The ':' scan tests the byte already loaded before loading buffer[colon+1] and counting it, which is retail's order at 0x004B1484-0x004B1490; the local buffer is 0x80 bytes and uninitialised exactly as retail's frame is.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: The handler's EAX is returned only on the depth==0 path; the two error branches never return, matching retail's jmp $ self-loops.

limitations: Runtime unobserved; reachable only through the device-open wrappers behind the startup boundary.

The device table has no transcribed registrar (retail 0x004B1B90 is missing), so the five records stay zeroed and every dispatch currently reports the device as not present. That is the honest state, not a filled-in table.
The handler contract (four arguments, int32 EAX) is established by the call sequence only; no device handler is transcribed yet.
The no-':' path passes &buffer[strlen+1], which is an uninitialised stack byte, exactly as retail does; what handlers do with it is unproven.

The catalog name Sys_IllegalDeviceNameInP is contradicted: the bytes are the device-path dispatcher that contains the illegal-name error branch, so the address-suffixed placeholder is kept and no rename is claimed.
